title: The Letter Scales
subtitle: 引力物理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 引力物理（宇宙探索·引力与物理）
meta: 主题语境：引力物理（宇宙探索·引力与物理）　|　核心词汇：weight　|　正文 380 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 weight 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: My grandfather kept a pair of letter scales on the hall table and a lump of brass in the drawer marked 20g, which we were forbidden to touch. The ① weight of a letter, he explained, decided what it cost and, more importantly, whether it was worth sending at all. I was nine and thought this was about money, and about the weight of a stamp. He was a physics teacher and it was never about money.

He taught me the difference properly, on the kitchen floor, with a bag of sugar. The ② weight of the bag, he said, is the pull of the earth on it; the mass is the sugar. Take the bag to the moon and the sugar stays, the ③ weight goes down to a sixth, and the recipe does not change. He ④ weighted the bag with a clip so it would sit still on the scales, and I have never since confused the two words.

The scales were the serious instrument. A letter that ⑤ weighed twenty grams went for one stamp; twenty-one grams cost nearly twice as much, and my grandmother wrote for forty minutes to save a stamp. My grandfather, who knew the weight of every stamp in the drawer, never did, because the ⑥ weight of an argument in that house was decided by who was willing to go on longest, and she always was.

In 1981 he took me to the coast and showed me a ⑦ weight on a rope: a plumb line, hanging in a hotel hallway, still and true while the sea moved outside. Everything in that building, he said, is square because somebody trusted a weight on a string. The ⑧ weight of the brass was irrelevant; what mattered was that it hung, and that gravity, unlike most things, is the same every morning.

I have his scales now, and the brass, and the clip. I have never weighed a letter. What I have done, more often than I can count, is put something on the scales and ask what ⑨ weight it has — meaning, usually, how much a decision will cost me to carry. ⑩ Weight, I have concluded, is the only physical quantity that doubles as a moral one, and the only one a child can learn from a bag of sugar.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 重量；分量（受引力作用的力）
B. n. 重量单位；砝码；秤砣
C. n. 重物；压东西的东西（铅垂、镇纸）
D. v. 加重量于；压住（weight sth）
F. n. 重压；负担（比喻义）
G. n. 分量；影响力；分量轻重（比喻义）
H. n. 重要性；严重性（the weight of）

items.q: the weight goes down to a sixth
He weighted the bag with a clip
A letter that weighed twenty grams
the weight of an argument in that house
showed me a weight on a rope
The weight of the brass was irrelevant
Weight, I have concluded, is the only physical quantity

answers.why: 指信的“重量”，即地球对它的引力，决定邮资。
指袋子所受的“重量”（地球引力），与 mass（质量）相对。
同样是物理量，说到了月球上重量变成六分之一。
weight 作动词，意为“加重量压住”，指用夹子把糖袋压稳在秤上。
weigh 作动词，意为“重达、称重”，说二十克只需一张邮票。
the weight of an argument 指争论中谁的“分量、影响力”更大。
指绳上挂的“重物”，即铅垂，靠它把楼房校直。
指那块黄铜作为“砝码、秤砣”的重量本身并不重要，重要的是它悬着。
比喻义，指一个决定要背负的“重压、负担”。
此处 weight 抽象为“重要性、分量”，说它兼具物理与道德两义。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 信的重量决定邮资，也决定它值不值得寄。（weight）

他用夹子把袋子压稳在秤上。（weight v.）
二十克的信只需一张邮票。（weigh v.）
楼里的一切都是方的，因为有人信一根绳上的重物。（weight）
我问的是：这个决定背起来有多重。（weight）
answers: The weight of a letter decides what it costs and whether it is worth sending.
The weight of the bag is the pull of the earth on it; the mass is the sugar.
He weighted the bag with a clip so it would sit still on the scales.
A letter that weighed twenty grams went for one stamp.
Everything in that building is square because somebody trusted a weight on a string.
What I ask is how much weight the decision will cost me to carry.
